0.label: double_spiral_knot_right
0.description: The right part of the band of double-spiral knots between the figures and the lizard, on the middle of the post.
0.iconography: Part of one knot band (with #1 and #2) dividing the figure register from the reptile register.

1.label: double_spiral_knot_left
1.description: The left part of the same knot band: two volutes coiling in opposite directions.
1.iconography: See #0 — one band cut into three boxes.

2.label: knot_band_slice
2.description: A narrow slice through the middle of the knot band between #1 and #0.
2.iconography: Not a separate motif — a strip of the same band.

3.label: lizard_figure_left
3.description: The left of two mirrored figures in the upper register: arms bent up with spread fingers, knees out, a dotted line from neck to groin that splits into an arch between the legs; the head is lost to a hole in the wood.
3.iconography: Its splayed pose and dotted spine match the lizard below (#5): a human–reptile figure or a person shown in a lizard's posture. Lizards and crocodiles carry royal and water power (Olókun) and appear in Ife origin stories.

4.label: lizard_figure_right
4.description: The right of the mirrored pair: a large head with striated 'rays', lozenge eyes and pointed ears, arms raised, dotted spine splitting into an arch between the legs.
4.iconography: The same radiating head as the lizard (#5) marks the pair as reptile-like beings — possibly masked men or guardian spirits. A mirrored pair at the top of a post works as a guardian couple.

5.label: lizard_crossing_register
5.description: A lizard or crocodile lying across the post below the knot band, seen from above: splayed bent legs, dotted spine, and a radiating striated head at the right.
5.iconography: A reptile — agama lizard or crocodile. It is the key that unlocks the figures above, which share its spine and head.

6.label: double_spiral_knot_lower
6.description: The broad lower band of double-spiral knots, holed by damage, closing the carved face.
6.iconography: The lowest binding band; its twin runs at the top of the post (undetected).

panel.title: Modakeke post: mirrored lizard-figures above a lizard, between knot bands
panel.summary: A post face with bands of double-spiral knots dividing two registers: a mirrored pair of figures with raised arms and dotted spines above, and a single lizard or crocodile lying across the post below.

register_readings.reading: Two mirrored lizard-like figures with raised arms and radiating heads.
A knot band dividing figures from reptile.
A lizard or crocodile crossing the post.

panel.composition: Knot bands alternate with figural registers. The upper pair is mirrored about the post's axis; the reptile below lies across it.
panel.narrative: The post pairs two reptile-like guardians with a lizard, the three sharing a dotted spine and radiating head. It may picture people taking a reptile's form — the powers of water and earth that guard a household or shrine — rather than a scene. The old reading took the pair for snake-holders or leopard-men; the shared spine points to the lizard.
panel.hypotheses: Does not bear on 'chronicle'. The knot bands are ornament, not obviously counted.
cross_panel_links: Reptile seen from above: EBA-Div_00311_panel_02 and the drawn trays KBA_10300, KBA_10305.
Same plate as FoA_04-5578 panels 00 and 01 (Modakeke).
uncertainties: The head of #3 is destroyed; the figures could be human dancers rather than hybrids.
#0-#2 are one knot band split into three boxes.
